semantics.ownership: A projection belongs to its containing form. Only the event envelope carries session, turn, iteration and form_index. Activity is not a View and never enters model context.
semantics.delivery: Each block.activity is a complete replacement, not a delta. Envelope seq orders revisions. Reconnect replays the latest replacement; settled evidence is durable.
semantics.lifecycle: The engine allocates invocation identity and entry sequence, records running before execution, and exactly one succeeded, failed or cancelled result. Presentation cannot control the operation.
semantics.counts: Counts describe observed invocations, including omitted rows. Group rows are presentation, not additional invocations. omitted.by_classification counts omitted evidence by signal. Readers group adjacent top-level rows by operation_groups in sequence order; unknown operations stay separate. A group keeps its first row identity (the first child for an engine shell group). Labels, presenters and states never establish adjacency. Shell polling children remain evidence of one command, not more commands.
semantics.bounds: Redact credential-bearing structured fields before summarizing; enforce UTF-8 byte limits. Row ids are globally unique within a projection. At most max_rows top-level rows and max_depth child edges. Omission is explicit, never invented success.
semantics.declaration: Symbols publish a presentation: headline, one-line summary, content blocks and optional sections of the same headline/summary/content shape. Headline and summary remain visible when collapsed; only content is disclosed. Up to 8 sections, 32 blocks in total and 32 KiB per replacement; each headline and summary is at most 512 UTF-8 bytes. Content includes headings, Markdown, tables, code, diffs, attachment references and progress. The engine alone owns identity, timing and outcome; presentation failures never alter tool results.
